conflicts.point: Whether pre-training license mandates effectively contain systemic risks or merely impose prohibitive compliance costs on open-source developers while missing distributed evasion tactics.

positions.stance: Pre-training licenses establish necessary safety baselines for massive training runs without burdening smaller developers who operate below statutory compute thresholds.
Licensing mandates impose heavy administrative costs that penalize open-source teams while failing to stop bad actors from using decentralized multi-agent hardware.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-training license mandates effectively contain systemic risks or merely impose prohibitive compliance costs on open-source developers while missing distributed evasion tactics.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic and accelerationist position accounts for both technical evasion tactics and the economic realities of cloud compute markets. Safety advocates correctly point out that hardware ownership is concentrated, but they underestimate how fixed administrative costs burden open-source developers and fail to stop distributed training schemes.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that Department of Commerce licensing can successfully track and intercept distributed multi-agent training runs without stifling open-source ecosystems would reverse this assessment.
